expects.rule: The product is shown in use within the first two screens: a real code sample, an install command, a product panel or a working demo, not only a slogan.
Documentation is in the primary navigation and one click from the home page, with a quickstart that ends in a working result.
The page names what it replaces or competes with, or the job it does, so an evaluator places it within seconds.
Code blocks are real text that can be selected and copied, with a copy button, a language switcher and syntax colours that keep a readable contrast.
Free start and sales contact both exist as paths: a self-serve sign-up and a talk-to-sales link.
Pricing, limits, status and changelog are public and linked from the header or footer.
The content is also readable by agents and scripts: plain text or markdown without scripts, stable headings, and no content hidden behind interaction.

traits: Header carries a Sign in or Log in link and one filled button on 8 of 8 sites; Docs is a header item on 6 of 8 (Resend, Clerk, Supabase, Neon, Sentry, and Vercel's Resources menu aside).
A mono face appears in the CSS of 6 of 8 sites (Resend, Clerk, Vercel, Neon, Railway, Sentry) next to Inter or Geist for text.
A real code block or command is visible on 0 of 8 first screens; 3 of 8 show a product panel (Clerk, Railway, Sentry), the rest art, a logo mark or a gradient.
Dark surfaces on 4 of 8 (Resend, Neon, Railway, Sentry); white or light grey on 4 of 8 (Stripe, Clerk, Vercel, Supabase).
Two buttons in the first screen on 8 of 8: one filled sign-up or deploy action and one docs, demo or sales action.
Headlines run 4 to 9 words at 40 to 96px; 2 of 8 are set in a serif (Resend, Railway).
An agent angle (MCP, prompt, agents) shows on the first screen on 5 of 8 (Stripe, Clerk, Vercel, Neon, Railway).
Proof on the first screen: a logo row on 2 of 8 (Stripe, Vercel) or a GitHub star count in the header on 2 of 8 (Supabase, Neon).

sites.name: Stripe
sites.why: Shown here in French. White page with an announcement bar, a 40px two-tone headline in a sans (sohne-var) over a full-bleed ribbon of orange, pink and violet, a purple start button beside a Google sign-up, and a scrolling row of customer logos. A live counter of share of world GDP sits above the title.

avoid: A hero with a stock photo of developers or a floating 3D cube and no code, command or demo.
Terminal or code screenshots saved as images, which cannot be copied or read by screen readers.
The same dark gradient, glowing grid and neon accent as every other developer site, with no product-specific visual.
Documentation behind a sign-up wall, or only a Book a demo button for a tool developers try themselves.
Claims such as "10x faster" with no benchmark, number or method.
A command that is shown but cannot be copied in one click, or code samples in only one language when SDKs exist for several.
